headline: Growth accelerates and cash flow surges, profit slips
summary_short: DoorDash's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 35.6% y/y to $4,454M on 27% order growth to 970 million, while GAAP net income fell 29.8% y/y to $200M on higher R&D and G&A spending; the company's own Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) rose 40% y/y to $914M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 35.6% y/y (24% y/y excluding Deliveroo) as Total Orders rose 27% y/y to 970M and Marketplace GOV rose 36% y/y to $33.1B. GAAP net income fell 29.8% y/y to $200M (though up 8.7% q/q) as R&D (+52% y/y) and G&A (+39% y/y, including higher legal/tax/regulatory settlement costs) outpaced revenue growth. Management's own Free Cash Flow was $742M, up 109% y/y. Cash fell 3.3% q/q to $4,424M and equity fell 2.7% q/q to $9,921M on $1,049M of YTD share buybacks. For Q3 2026 the company guided Marketplace GOV to $33.0-34.0B and Adjusted EBITDA to $950-1,100M, and flagged an expected Q4 Adjusted-EBITDA-margin decline from seasonal Dasher costs, insurance, and tech/autonomy investment.

drivers.explanation: Total Orders grew 27% y/y and Marketplace GOV 36% y/y, driven by consumer growth, higher average order value, and the Deliveroo acquisition; ex-Deliveroo revenue growth was 24% y/y.
Y/y decline driven by increases in R&D and G&A expense, including higher legal, tax, and regulatory settlement costs and personnel-related compensation, which outpaced revenue growth.

Company's own Adjusted EBITDA of $914M was described as 'well above' expectation, driven by GOV growth and improving unit economics at Wolt and Deliveroo; note this shard's EBITDA figure ($453M) is GAAP-based and not comparable to that non-GAAP figure.

Company guided Q3 2026 Marketplace GOV to $33.0-34.0B and Adjusted EBITDA to $950-1,100M, and expects a Q4 Adjusted-EBITDA-margin decline from seasonal Dasher costs, insurance, and tech/autonomy investment.
